Title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code

URL Source: https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-7-sonnet

Published Time: 2025-02-24T17:00:00.000Z

Markdown Content:
Today, we’re announcing Claude 3.7 Sonnet, our most intelligent model to date and the first hybrid reasoning model on the market.

Claude 3.7 Sonnet shows particularly strong improvements in coding and front-end web development. Along with the model, we’re also introducing Claude Code, a command line tool for agentic coding.

![Image 1: Screen showing Claude Code onboarding](https://www.anthropic.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww-cdn.anthropic.com%2Fimages%2Fclaude-code.png&w=3840&q=75)

Claude 3.7 Sonnet is now available on all Claude plans, the Claude Developer Platform, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud’s Vertex AI.

Claude 3.7 Sonnet: Frontier reasoning made practical
----------------------------------------------------

We’ve developed Claude 3.7 Sonnet with a different philosophy from other reasoning models on the market. Just as humans use a single brain for both quick responses and deep reflection, we believe reasoning should be an integrated capability of frontier models rather than a separate model entirely.

Claude 3.7 Sonnet is both an ordinary LLM and a reasoning model in one. In standard mode, Claude 3.7 Sonnet represents an upgraded version of Claude 3.5 Sonnet. In extended thinking mode, it self-reflects before answering, which improves its performance on math, physics, instruction-following, coding, and many other tasks.

When using Claude 3.7 Sonnet through the API, users can control the budget for thinking and trade off speed for quality of answer.

Early testing demonstrated Claude’s leadership in coding capabilities across the board. Cursor noted Claude is once again best-in-class for real-world coding tasks. Vercel highlighted Claude’s precision for complex agent workflows.

Since June 2024, Sonnet has been the preferred model for developers worldwide. Today, we're empowering developers further by introducing Claude Code in a limited research preview.
